ai.literal: Firmness of action is called a person's firmness of mind; other all are different.
ai.translation: What is called firmness in action is simply a person's firmness of mind. All other things are secondary.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்து முடிக்கும் உறுதி என்பது ஒருவனுடைய மன உறுதியே ஆகும்; மற்றவை எல்லாம் அதற்கு ஈடாகாத வேறுபட்டவைகளே.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines what it truly means to be resolute in one's actions. The phrase 'வினைத்திட்பம்' (firmness of action) is directly equated to 'மனத்திட்பம்' (firmness of mind), showing that outward success relies entirely on inner conviction. The word 'பிற' (other or different) is used here to mean that all other resources or advantages are secondary and belong to a different, lesser category. Thus, true strength in any undertaking comes from mental resolve rather than external factors.

ai.literal: Obstacle avoiding, after occurring not faltering, of these two the way, they say, of the analyzed ones the principle.
ai.translation: Avoiding obstacles, and not faltering when they do occur—these two are the guiding principles of those who have analyzed the way of action.
ai.modern: இடையூறுகள் வராமல் தவிர்ப்பதும், வந்தபின் மனம் தளராமல் இருப்பதும் ஆகிய இவ்விரண்டுமே செயல்களை ஆராய்ந்தவர்களின் கொள்கை என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core mindset required for firmness in action. First, one must proactively avoid obstacles (ஊறு ஒரால்). Second, if obstacles still occur despite one's best efforts, one must not lose heart or falter (உற்றபின் ஒல்காமை). The wise who have deeply analyzed the nature of action declare that mastering these two paths is the ultimate guiding principle (கோள்).

ai.literal: To become known at the end, doing what is fit, is capability; if it becomes known in the middle, unremovable sorrow it will give.
ai.translation: True capability is executing a fitting task so that it becomes known only upon its completion. If it is revealed midway, it will cause inescapable sorrow.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலை அதன் முடிவில் வெளிப்படும்படியாகச் செய்து முடிப்பதே திறமையாகும். இடையில் அச்செயல் வெளிப்பட்டால் அது நீங்காத துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of secrecy and timing in executing a plan. The word 'ஆண்மை' (manliness or capability) here refers to the strength of character required to keep a plan concealed until it is successfully completed. The verb 'கொட்க' means to become known or revealed. If a fitting action is exposed in the middle ('இடைக்கொட்கின்') before completion, obstacles can easily thwart it. Such a premature revelation will result in 'எற்றா விழுமம்', meaning an inescapable or unremovable sorrow.

ai.literal: Saying to anyone easy things; difficult things they are spoken manner doing.
ai.translation: Telling others how to act is easy for anyone. Doing the deed exactly as spoken is difficult.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலை இப்படிச் செய்ய வேண்டும் என்று சொல்வது யாருக்கும் எளிதானது. ஆனால் சொல்லியபடியே அந்தச் செயலைச் செய்து முடிப்பது மிகவும் கடினமானது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the ease of giving advice with the difficulty of execution. The word 'collutal' (saying) is paired with 'eḷiya' (easy things), showing that anyone can easily talk about how a task should be done. However, 'ceyal' (doing) exactly in the 'vaṇṇam' (manner) it was spoken is described as 'ariya' (difficult things). True firmness in action requires matching one's deeds to one's words.

ai.literal: Greatness having attained, the excellent ones' firmness of action, reaching the king, will be esteemed.
ai.translation: The firmness in action of those who have attained greatness and excellence will reach the king and be highly esteemed.
ai.modern: பெருமை அடைந்து சிறந்தவர்களின் செயல் உறுதியானது அரசனிடம் சென்று சேர்ந்து அவனால் பெரிதும் மதிக்கப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights how resolute action elevates a person's standing. The phrase 'வீறு எய்தி மாண்டார்' refers to those who have attained greatness through their excellence. Their firmness in action does not go unnoticed; it reaches the ruler and earns their deep respect. The word 'ஊறு' here means reaching or firmly establishing oneself, chosen over its other common meaning of harm, to show how their reputation successfully reaches the king.

ai.literal: The things intended, as intended, they will attain, those who intended, firm people, to become, if they achieve.
ai.translation: Those who plan will achieve exactly what they planned, if they possess the firmness of mind to carry it out.
ai.modern: எண்ணியவர்கள் மன உறுதி உடையவர்களாக இருக்கப் பெற்றால், அவர்கள் எண்ணிய செயல்களை எண்ணியபடியே அடைவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that mere planning is not enough; firmness of mind is required to see a plan through. The word 'எண்ணிய' refers to the goals or actions planned, while 'எண்ணியாங்கு' means achieving them exactly as envisioned. The condition for this success is 'திண்ணியர் ஆகப் பெறின்', meaning one must possess unwavering determination.

ai.literal: Having seen the form, not despising is needed; to the rolling large chariot, people like the axle-pin it possesses.
ai.translation: Do not underestimate anyone based on their appearance. The world possesses people who are as crucial as the small linchpin to a massive, rolling chariot.
ai.modern: ஒருவரின் தோற்றத்தைக் கண்டு அவரைச் சாதாரணமாக எண்ணி இகழக்கூடாது. உருண்டோடும் பெரிய தேருக்குச் சிறிய அச்சாணி எவ்வளவு முக்கியமோ, அதுபோன்ற ஆற்றல் உடையவர்கள் இவ்வுலகில் உள்ளனர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against judging a person's capability by their physical appearance. A chariot may be massive and impressive as it rolls along, but its movement depends entirely on a small linchpin holding the axle together. Similarly, people who appear small or unassuming may possess the crucial strength and firmness of action needed to sustain great enterprises. The word 'அச்சாணி' (linchpin) perfectly captures how immense power and stability can reside in a small, unpretentious form.

ai.literal: Without confusion decided in the action, without wavering, delay having discarded, one should do.
ai.translation: Once an action has been decided upon with a clear mind, one should execute it without wavering and without any delay.
ai.modern: மனக்குழப்பம் இல்லாமல் ஆராய்ந்து முடிவு செய்த ஒரு செயலை, பின்பு எந்தத் தயக்கமும் இல்லாமல் காலதாமதத்தை விலக்கிச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of resolute execution once a decision is made. The word 'கலங்காது' (without confusion) describes the clear state of mind required when choosing a course of action. Once the deed is 'கண்ட' (decided or clearly seen), the focus shifts entirely to execution. The words 'துளங்காது' (without wavering) and 'தூக்கம் கடிந்து' (discarding delay) instruct the doer to act with unwavering firmness and promptness. Here, the word 'தூக்கம்' (which normally means sleep) is used in the specific sense of delay or procrastination.

ai.literal: Suffering to-experience even-if-comes, let-one-do, resolve having-made-firm, joy yielding action.
ai.translation: Even if it brings great suffering, one should form a firm resolve and perform the action that will ultimately yield joy.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்யும்போது மிகுந்த துன்பம் வந்தாலும், மன உறுதியைக் கொண்டு, முடிவில் இன்பம் தரக்கூடிய அச்செயலைச் செய்து முடிக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of perseverance and firm resolve when undertaking a beneficial task. The phrase 'இன்பம் பயக்கும் வினை' refers to an action that will ultimately produce good results or lasting happiness. Even if executing this action brings intense immediate suffering ('துன்பம் உற வரினும்'), the doer must gather their determination ('துணிவு ஆற்றி') and see it through. The focus is on enduring temporary hardship for the sake of a permanent positive outcome.

ai.literal: Whatever-firmness attained even-if, action-firmness those-who-lack desires-not the-world.
ai.translation: Even if they possess every other kind of firmness, the world will not value those who lack firmness in action.
ai.modern: வேறு எவ்வளவு வலிமைகளை அடைந்திருந்தாலும், செயலில் உறுதி இல்லாதவர்களை இந்த உலகம் மதிக்காது.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme importance of firmness in action. The phrase 'எனைத்திட்பம்' refers to any other kind of strength or firmness, such as wealth, military power, or intellect. Even if a person possesses all these, the world ('உலகு') will not value or respect them ('வேண்டாது') if they lack 'வினைத்திட்பம்'—the resolute determination to carry out an action to its end. The repetition of 'திட்பம்' (firmness) and 'வேண்டு' (desire/value) creates a strong contrast between what one might have and what the world truly demands.
